title: Deploying AI Models on Edge GPUs: The Practical Challenges
gist: Forum post promoting an 11 November Imagination Technologies webinar on optimising LLM deployment on edge GPUs; it argues getting a model running via llama.cpp is easy but optimising throughput, memory and quantisation under edge power/cost constraints is the real work.

insights.claim: Getting a large language model running on an edge platform is relatively easy today because open-source frameworks such as llama.cpp allow download, inference and demonstration within minutes.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Low barrier to edge LLM demos shifts differentiation to optimisation tooling and hardware efficiency.
insights.locator: Getting a large language model running

insights.claim: An edge LLM deployment may run correctly yet deliver disappointing throughput, consume more memory than expected, or leave significant performance untapped, requiring analysis of how the workload interacts with the hardware and software stack.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Software optimisation expertise is a bottleneck for edge AI adoption.
insights.quote: Optimising that deployment is where the real work begins.

insights.claim: Edge AI deployment challenges are becoming more relevant because memory, power and cost constraints on edge devices are far stricter than in the datacentre.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Edge inference favours efficient quantisation and GPU offload strategies over raw compute.
insights.locator: These challenges are becoming increasingly relevant

insights.claim: Imagination Technologies will host a webinar on 11 November covering model quantisation, GPU offloading strategies and performance analysis for AI models on edge GPU platforms using open-source software.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Imagination is positioning its GPU IP for edge AI inference.
insights.locator: In an upcoming webinar on 11 November
